A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, equations, tables and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained content despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical results and explanatory tables. Neither the main text nor Appendices A–F report original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian simulations in Section 3.2 and Figure 1, plus synthetic exponential-family estimation experiments in Appendix G and Figure 2.

M1.justification: The f-NCE, alpha-CentNCE and f-CondNCE objectives, centering transformation and local formulations are retained. v2 makes K conditional draws explicit as a sampling parameter for the existing CondNCE estimator.

E1.justification: v2 introduces actual evaluation on two synthetic settings: one-dimensional Gaussian mean estimation and parameter recovery for a bounded quadratic exponential family on [-1,1]^p. v1 contains no empirical dataset or task evaluation.

E2.justification: Appendix G introduces empirical comparisons involving LogNCE, asymmetric power NCE with alpha=0.25, asymmetric inverse-log NCE and alpha-CentNCE with alpha=0.5. It also reports evaluating f1-NCE and CNCE without convergence. These methods appeared only analytically in v1.

E3.justification: New protocols include Gaussian objective-derivative evaluation with N=10^4 and sweeps over epsilon and K. Appendix G evaluates Frobenius parameter error for p={11,13,15,17,19}, using subsamples from 0.04N to 0.64N of N=10^5 and fixed optimization budgets.

E4.justification: Figure 1 adds an empirical sensitivity analysis of CondNCE across six noise scales and four conditional-sample counts, supplementing v1's analytical discussion. Figure 2 additionally examines estimation-error scaling with sample size and dimension.

E5.justification: Appendix G newly reports five repetitions with random subsamples per configuration, and Figure 2 displays error bars. Their statistical meaning is not defined, and seeds, confidence intervals and significance tests are not supplied.

E6.justification: v2 adds noise-dependent derivative curves, convergence curves for four estimators and reported nonconvergence of f1-NCE and CNCE. Figure 2 labels fitted exponents between -0.33 and -0.44, although Appendix G describes n^-1/2 convergence. These are new outcomes, with no corresponding empirical results in v1.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.3 changes its bounding constants to CondNCE-specific constants defined over (rho_min/rho_max, rho_max/rho_min), with corresponding revisions in Appendix D.3. Most theory remains unchanged; v2's Theorem 4.4 restates v1's Theorem D.1 in the main text.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal unification and convergence contributions are retained. Introduction contribution 3 now qualifies small-noise variance divergence by insufficient conditional samples, and the conclusion explicitly calls for further high-dimensional empirical investigation.

C2.justification: Appendix G newly interprets observed f1-NCE and CNCE nonconvergence as an unresolved discrepancy with theoretical guarantees, motivating further empirical investigation. The conditional-sample tradeoff itself was already acknowledged in v1 Remark 3.4.

D1.justification: v2 adds experimental implementation information absent from v1: the synthetic parameter matrix, 100-bin discretization per axis, Frobenius regularization with weight 0.01, and 1,000 gradient steps using learning rate 0.1 except 1.0 for LogNCE. These provide a substantial new experimental recipe, although code and hardware information remain absent.

R1.justification: The same 35 cited works and substantive estimator connections are retained. The literature positioning remains centered on unifying existing estimators and clarifying CondNCE's relationship to score matching; author-year citations and reference relocation are presentation changes.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited prose clarifications, shortens headings and adds section introductions and a main-text proof sketch. References move before the appendices, and funding and impact statements are added. Most existing prose and the appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, with equations and tables repositioned and reformatted. v2 adds the 24-panel Figure 1 and four-panel Figure 2 while retaining the five original tables.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful empirical checks and a more precise small-noise claim to v1's theoretical treatment; the main-text proof sketch also improves accessibility. The gains are limited by unexplained estimator nonconvergence and Appendix G's n^-1/2 characterization despite Figure 2's fitted exponents of -0.33 to -0.44. Overall, the added evidence and qualifications provide a modest improvement.
